q: When new content arrives, what is the unit that triggers extraction?
a: Every message pair (user turn + assistant turn), incrementally.

q: What context should the extractor see besides the new content?
a: Rolling async conversation summary + last 10 messages.

q: Who decides what is salient enough to store?
a: An LLM prompt asking for salient facts. Untyped, uncapped.

q: Whose facts get retained?
a: Both speakers, symmetric stores (speaker_1_memories, speaker_2_memories).

q: When does extraction run relative to the request?
a: Synchronously per pair; summary refresh async. (They attack Zep for async lag.)

q: What shape does a stored memory take?
a: A dense natural-language sentence (Mem0); entity–relation triplets (Mem0g).

q: What links a memory to where it came from?
a: Nothing in base Mem0. Mem0g keeps a creation timestamp on nodes. (Notably LOCOMO's own baseline system does keep dialog-turn refs — Mem0 dropped that.)

q: How much confidence is a memory entitled to?
a: One flat tier. Everything is asserted.

q: May the extractor infer beyond what was said?
a: Yes, explicitly: Mem0g prompts the LLM to reason about "implicit information".

q: Is a hypothesis representable at all?
a: No grammar for it. Storage can only assert.

q: When a new fact contradicts a stored one, what resolves it?
a: An LLM function-call picks ADD / UPDATE / DELETE / NOOP at write time.

q: Where does a contradicted memory go?
a: Base Mem0: physically deleted. Mem0g: marked invalid, retained for temporal reasoning.

q: Which existing memories are checked for conflict?
a: Top-s = 10 by embedding similarity to the candidate.

q: What can the user do about a memory directly?
a: Nothing. Correction only via saying something contradictory in a later turn.

q: What happens to a memory nobody re-observes?
a: Nothing. Memories persist forever unless contradicted.

q: Can a memory change status without new content?
a: No. Status is a function of content only.

q: How are memories found at query time?
a: Embedding top-k over memory strings; Mem0g adds entity-anchored subgraph + triplet similarity above threshold t.

q: What ranks a memory above another?
a: Cosine similarity alone. No recency prior, no evidence weight, no tier.

q: Is everything retrieved allowed to be said?
a: Yes — no separation. Retrieved ⇒ in prompt ⇒ sayable.

q: Do different surfaces get different memory rights?
a: No. One store, one path.

q: What does the user see about how an answer was produced?
a: Nothing. No trace, no sources, no "what was withheld".

q: What should the system do when memory doesn't contain the answer?
a: Answer anyway. The generation prompt mandates an answer "less than 5-6 words". The unanswerable question category was removed from the evaluation.

q: How much of the user's attention may the system spend?
a: Question never arises; the system never asks anything.

q: What model does the extraction and update?
a: GPT-4o-mini for everything, temperature 0.
